# In what coordinate system should the first six dimensions of Pinocchio's aba() be interpreted when returning floating base generalized acceleration?

> **Current answer:** The original author defined the output as a=[base-frame linear acceleration, base-frame angular acceleration, joint accelerations], and the maintainer confirmed it is correct. Therefore, cannot directly take the first six dimensions of aba as world-frame base acceleration. The thread did not provide a local-to-world acceleration transformation, and did not clarify the difference between classical and spatial acceleration. When these quantities are involved, they must be verified against the target API definition.

## Key terms

- Joint body algorithm (ABA) (关节体算法)
- Generalized acceleration (广义加速度)
- Local joint frame (局部关节坐标系)
- Spatial acceleration (空间加速度)

## Problem and symptoms

- What coordinate system should the first six dimensions of aba() be interpreted in when returning floating base generalized acceleration?
- The user is aware of the floating base linear velocity components in the local joint frame, but is uncertain whether the acceleration is expressed in the same way.

## Environment

- 2022 Pinocchio floating-base dynamics; specific version and robot not mentioned.

## Priority diagnostics

- Interpreted aba as a generalized acceleration in the generalized space of the base local frame, and verified the root joint local coordinate convention.

## Possible causes

- Misinterpretation of generalized acceleration as a world-frame second-order position derivative.

## Attempts

- The author listed a=[local base linear acceleration, local base angular acceleration, joint accelerations], and the maintainer confirmed it.

## Effective fixes

- Interpreted the first six dimensions of aba as base local frame generalized acceleration; explicit world-frame transformation is required when world-frame quantities are needed.

## Result

- The maintainer confirmed the local coordinate interpretation of the first six dimensions of aba is correct.
